body: We do not accept AI authored PRs, and agent created PRs are not accepted, please see [this](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/development/contribution_rules.html#for-contributors)

> We do not accept AI authored PRs, and agent created PRs are not accepted, please see [this](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/development/contribution_rules.html#for-contributors)

I added that as required by your policies to denote any AI usage and I manually cleaned it all up (this took hours of manual work and to create the project) and I simplified it by removing all of the AI junk and slop.  Your policies require the disclosure of AI usage so I added that as required.  Then on top of that you don't appreciate any of that work I did to double check everything and just close it immediately.

So what should I do now?
So you are saying you personally wrote all the code and opened the PR yourself and added a disclosure that it was made by an autonomous agent? That makes no sense...

> So you are saying you personally wrote all the code and opened the PR yourself and added a disclosure that it was made by an autonomous agent? That makes no sense...

AI was used to discover the issue and what causes it.  I applied a work-around in the mean-time for my project.  I then asked AI to dig into the godot-engine source and to fix it properly.  It did that and created a bunch of comments and AI slop.  I cleaned that up manually.  I ran the tests again and everything was still the same.  I then asked it to generate the example project difference scripts and to generate the difference image.  I then created the PR (manually on github's website because I don't allow AI to submit PRs or do things on my github account on by behalf). It said that because AI was used to generate some of this work that it must be disclosed due to your policies.  So I did that and then you closed it immediately because of my disclosure.  Are you encouraging people to not disclose AI usage from now on when they use it to help them solve issues with the engine?  How does this help improve the community?  This seems more like a personal anti-AI issue rather than let's improve the engine and make things better and be sure to clearly disclose AI usage (according to your policies)?

So I ask once again, "So what should I do now?".

It's pretty weird to say "[!INFO] AI disclosure: This contribution was authored by an autonomous AI agent (Claude Code), on behalf of a user, to fix 119879" when you made the PR, and wrote the code yourself.

We require contributors to disclose AI use this PR doesn't contain a disclosure, because it doesn't say what AI was used for according to the guidelines

It was closed because the PR description literally says it was authored by an autonomous agent and we don't allow that

So I now ask:
* Did you write the code yourself?
* Why did you add a disclosure claiming it was created by an autonomous agent on your behalf?

If the code in this PR was written by you, and you add a disclosure of what AI was used for and how, then it can be reopened, but in the future I'd suggest not making confusing PR descriptions that make them look like you didn't write them

"Did you write the code yourself?"
- as I stated, AI wrote sloppy code to fix the engine and I spent my time to clean it up.  So where do we draw the line?

"Why did you add a disclosure claiming it was created by an autonomous agent on your behalf?"
- as I stated, Opus 5.5 said I needed to add that disclosure to the top of the PR because AI was used in figuring out the issue and in the generation of the example project scripts and image.

So I'm going to leave it here because I have to get to work at my day job and whether or not you guys accept my work is up to you.  At least it is documented here for others.

That explains the disclosure part, you asked your agent to process the repo and it spat out the instructions for an agent trying to post to Godot, it is obviously not for humans

This is not a valid PR as it was not human authored, which is clarified in the guidelines

For the future I'd suggest reading the guidelines for projects instead of letting your agent explain them to you, as that way you miss a lot, like what our guidelines require and what contributions we allow

If you're interested in contributing in the future please make sure to read the guidelines carefully, and best of luck

> So where do we draw the line?

For this, see [this](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/development/contribution_rules.html#for-contributors)

This pr is 17 lines of code changed, each very clear in what it's doing besides 2 which I might consider rewriting to be clearer to more novice users.

The explanation also tracks with where I expected the issue to lie (I suspected that queue_free was taking action mid-frame, given that waiting on the frame's end (my understanding of what await physics_frame/process_frame results in) before calling it resolved it)

I just never had the time to debug it further (given I had workarounds and only ever really Experimented with TAA and aren't actually actively using it) nor have I ever been too comfy digging too far into engine internals.

I'll be frank, it fixes a known issue (haven't built and tested yet, but I have no reason to doubt the claim) and the reasoning is Sound (And at it's core, Expected!), the Code is clear... I do not see a good reason to prohibit this PR.
My take on the reason for refusing this PR is... well Harry V. puts it best: "This is some BS"

**_Somewhat Off-topic segment_**
Oh and let me stop you right there, before you go "read the policy" I did, and segment by segment I do not see any substantial evidence of breaking the policy 
1) it's not a new feature
2) it changes one thing
3) it is clearly explained
4) it's easy to understand (and therefor I expect the OP understands it)
5) the policy prohibits AI for human to human communication but not for formatting and explicitly allows for translation which formatting can be considered
6) this doesn't look like an AI model just posted up a PR
7) this PR does not contain substantial pieces of code
8) I do not see any user facing GenAI content

therefor given everything stated so far, I would like to point out that it looks like you are failing to follow the 2nd expectation of Godot's Code of Conduct, which clearly states to always assume positive intentions from others.

I have not prohibited this PR:
> If the code in this PR was written by you, and you add a disclosure of what AI was used for and how, then it can be reopened

Thank you for your feedback but if you read through the thread you will find my clear explanation for my assumptions. OP decided to not proceed with this PR, regardless of any other factors, and is free to ask for this PR to be reopened if they make the required adjustments

I used prohibited in place of invalidate.

They have no adjustments to make?

here's the TLDR from what I understand of everything stated so far:

AI was used to figure out where the bug lies, it tried to take a stab at figuring it out, OP noted it was a mess he had to clean up. AI told him he needs to disclose AI usage, the Rules aren't perfectly clear on what formatting is required to use, so he doesn't know what to change regarding that and the AI didn't have any idea what to do either, hence the odd formatting.
AI was used to get some tests that do reproduce the problem, and do a before and after, and AI was used to form the Comparison from the results.
There are a few places where I feel like there's a lot of miscommunication taking place, as the responses back and forth were a bit cyclic for no apparent reason I can discern, and at the end of it he gave up and called it quits.
This conversation isn't productive, please leave it to OP to adjust based on my instructions, this is not the place to discuss the AI policy

Just to provide a bit of additional perspective here. 

We don't accept code authored by AI. Claude is literally given credit as Co-Author. **This PR is unacceptable for this reason alone.** 

We don't allow using AI to communicate on Github. That includes writing PR descriptions. This PR description is obviously written by Claude, it includes a ton of unnecessary information and is incorrect about the description of the problem. It wastes our time having to read through AI slop that is wrong and overly verbose. **This PR is unacceptable for this reason alone.**

We explicitly forbid allowing AI to open PRs your behalf. Which you clearly did since your agent fell for our trap intended to catch this case. **This PR is unacceptable for this reason alone.**

Don't play dumb here. You are wasting everyone's time by sticking to a story that is obviously untrue. 

Finally, and I say this last because I want to be clear that this PR was justifiably closed for improper AI usage, this is the wrong approach to fixing this bug. This PR is not mergable, regardless of whether an AI was involved or not. It is quite simply wrong. 

I'm sorry you wasted your tokens on this.

> Don't play dumb here. You are wasting everyone's time by sticking to a story that is obviously untrue.

Actually what I said was true and the CoAuthor in the git commit is because I told Opus to commit it to my local git repo with a proper message.  I then pushed it to my github fork and clicked on the Create Pull Request button and I took the huge description that Opus had and I cleaned it up and fixed context where I thought it was appropriate.  I copied that "AI disclosure" from Opus because it said it is required.  I didn't realize that the first line was meant to be the title and the second line is the notice bar, that was my mistake in copying it.  I added the description, table, zip files, and image file with a lot of portions taken from Opus and others from my edits.
 
> Finally, and I say this last because I want to be clear that this PR was justifiably closed for improper AI usage, this is the wrong approach to fixing this bug. This PR is not mergable, regardless of whether an AI was involved or not. It is quite simply wrong.

What is the correct way to fix this issue then?  Now that we know what causes it, it should be easy for someone with much more intimate knowledge to fix this properly.

> I'm sorry you wasted your tokens on this.

I'm sorry I wasted my time doing this and next time I won't waste my time to try to contribute work-arounds or bug-fixes that I discover.  It is not worth my time because I have a family with kids that I should be spending time with rather than trying to help you guys.  I wish I could get my 3 hours back and instead I should have just posted the work-around.  That time, from now on, will be better spent with family and not trying to help out others here because it is clearly not appreciated and it is quite toxic.

I'll remind you, specifically you clayjohn, that I have had previous dealings with you in 2023 for previous engine contributions and it is clear that it is just not appreciated.  I'm stating all of this here for the public record.

Even if your story is true, the way it shows to us (with Opus as co-author) it is impossible to tell how much is Opus and how much is your edits. Secondly it shows you did not read the Godot documentation as it clearly says AI coauthored PRs are not allowed. (And if you didn't realize the commit Opus made to your fork would show when you made a PR, then you don't understand git)
